title: S019 — Prior-judgment seeded Phase-A equivalence
description: Test whether the authoritative Phase A fixpoint can be seeded from the previous authoritative judgment map and still converge to exactly the same result as the from-scratch implementation.
result_summary: BLOCKED. Experiment A (complete prior-truth seeding) is NOT reference-equivalent: 26/400 steps diverge (6.5%). Breakdown: negateEvent 19/84, retractFact 2/32, severEdge 3/38, setFact 1/152, forceEvent 1/68, addEdge 0/26. Example: ev/treaty-of-ash ref=FALSE seeded=TRUE (stale TRUE). Negative control force->negate: ref=FALSE seeded=TRUE. EXACT CAUSE: Phase A is sticky ('if (current !== NEITHER) continue'), so a seeded decided value is never recomputed; a prior TRUE whose support the intervention removed is preserved forever. The reset to NEITHER is therefore semantically necessary for the current sticky Phase A. Seeding is sound only for monotone-increasing interventions. The required fix is an invalidation mechanism (a later experiment), which needs per-node decision provenance; the prior truth map alone is insufficient. No dirty queue, no invalidation, no selective recomputation, no cached fixpoint, no semantic rule change.

answers.Q3_stale_mechanism: sticky Phase A never recomputes a decided node, so a prior TRUE whose support was removed persists
answers.Q4_must_invalidate: every prior judgment whose support/override the intervention weakened (support removal, negateEvent, retractFact, severEdge, cycle creation)
answers.Q5_structural_invalidation: not from structure alone - 'support remains valid' needs per-node decision provenance
answers.Q6_reduces_reconsideration: no - it only changes starting values, and does so unsoundly
answers.Q7_global_mechanisms: Phase A global sticky closure and Phase B global unfounded-set shrink both remain
answers.Q8_incremental_with_global_barrier: not demonstrated; Phase A cannot become incremental without invalidation
answers.Q9_min_state: prior truth map PLUS per-node decision provenance (which support group/override decided it)
answers.Q10_genuine_engine: neither yet - naive seeding is a wrong full-propagation variant; a real engine first needs an invalidation mechanism

next_experiment: minimum sound invalidation mechanism for a preserved fixpoint - requires per-node decision provenance, not merely the prior judgment map.
limitations: Seed canons + 200-step random histories; the full adversarial corpus was not separately enumerated (Experiment A already failed).
Only sticky Phase A seeding was tested; seeded Phase B was not isolated.
Long-horizon, branch, determinism measurements not run (mechanism disqualified).
